```{python}
# | echo: false
# The "notebook" renderer defines the AMD module locally, so the figure works
# with no network. "notebook_connected" - the default - points requirejs at
# cdn.plot.ly instead, and requirejs gives up after 7 s.
import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"

PLOTLY_CONFIG = {"displaylogo": False, "responsive": True}
```

## What this deck shows

- **`.calc-slide`** - the derivation: equations and the values they use
- **`.plot-slide`** - the figure it produces, filling the slide
- The figure stays sized to its slide, so drag-to-zoom selects what you mean
- `Shift+D` switches the theme, and the figure repaints with it

Needs `jupyter`, `numpy` and `plotly`. The rail and theme toggle on their own
need none of that - see `demo.qmd`.

## Damped natural frequency {.calc-slide}

The calculation slide carries the derivation; the figure gets its own slide
after it, so neither has to make room for the other.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}

$$\omega_d = \omega_n\sqrt{1-\zeta^2} \tag{1}$$

$$x(t) = A e^{-\zeta\omega_n t}\sin(\omega_d t + \phi) \tag{2}$$

:::
::: {.column width="48%"}

| Symbol | Value | Unit |
|---|---:|---|
| $\omega_n$ | 12.0 | rad/s |
| $\zeta$ | 0.08 | – |
| $\omega_d$ | 11.96 | rad/s |
| $A$ | 1.0 | mm |

:::
:::

Equation (2) is what the next slide draws. Values above are the ones it uses,
so a number on the figure can be checked without leaving the deck.

::: {.notes}
Say what the calculation establishes, then move on - the figure is the point.
:::

## Damped free decay {.plot-slide}

```{python}
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go

wn, zeta, A = 12.0, 0.08, 1.0
wd = wn * np.sqrt(1 - zeta**2)
t = np.linspace(0, 3, 601)
envelope = A * np.exp(-zeta * wn * t)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_scatter(x=t, y=envelope * np.sin(wd * t), mode="lines",
                name="x(t)", line=dict(width=2))
fig.add_scatter(x=t, y=envelope, mode="lines", name="envelope",
                line=dict(width=1, dash="dot"))
fig.update_layout(
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=10, b=45),
    xaxis_title="Time, s",
    yaxis_title="Displacement, mm",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.08),
    height=560,
)
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```


::: {.plot-caption}
Drag a box on the figure to zoom; double-click to reset. The figure is sized
to the slide on every slide change, so the zoom region is the shape you see.
:::

::: {.notes}
This is the pair: calculation, then picture. Switch the theme with Shift+D and
the figure repaints - Plotly keeps its colours in the layout, not in CSS.
:::

## That is the pair

A calculation slide, then the picture it produces. A number on the figure can
be checked against the table without the figure slide carrying a wall of text.
